children: Canada mineral drilling firm's fiscal Q1 revenue rose 29% yr/yr to a record high
Company posted a net loss for fiscal Q1 due to higher costs and workforce investments
Company launched new share buyback program for up to 500,000 shares over 12 months
Company expects pricing adjustments and productivity improvements to progressively benefit profitability through fiscal 2027
Company anticipates new specialized drilling contract to contribute positively from H2 fiscal 2027
HIGHER DRILLING ACTIVITY - Co said increased drilling activity in Canada and South America drove revenue growth
COST PRESSURES - Co said profitability was hurt by inflation in production costs, higher wages, and increased investments in workforce training and development
LOWER PRODUCTIVITY - Co said a higher number of trainee drillers reduced drilling productivity, weighing on margins
HIGHER DEPRECIATION - Co said increased depreciation expenses from recent capital investments negatively impacted gross profit and margin
The stock recently traded at 5 times the next 12-month earnings vs. a P/E of 6 three months ago
